date: 16 Jan 1478 (as written; Florentine style would make it 1479)
title: Giovanni Mazzinghi's cipher letter of 16 January 1478, bare; the same cipher is glossed in MAP 72/170 a week later
correspondents: Giovanni Mazzinghi -> (the Medici; addressee not named on the page)
place: not stated (Rome likely: the sibling letter reports papal news)
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza LXXXIX, doc. 142 (old c. 149)
folio_note: One leaf, recto full of cipher (about 45 lines, some clear words between runs); verso blank but endorsed "1478 ... adi 16 di gennaio ... Gio. Mazinghi" and "Cifra". Inventory vol. 3: "Giovanni Mazzinghi. (cifrato). s. l., 1478 gen. 16, n. 142".
status: No decipherment on, over or beside the cipher (checked at 1600 px). The sign set (x, ‡, H, =, 5-like signs) is the one of MAP LXXII doc. 170 (23 Jan 1478), which carries a full interlinear decipherment.
why: A pre-1497 Florentine cipher letter of the Medici circle in the months around the Pazzi conspiracy, unread on the page, with a glossed sibling in the same system: a short route to a reading.
verify: Transcribe MAP 72/170, build the key from its interlinear pairs, apply it to 89/142; check the date style and Mazzinghi's post (Rome?) in the letter itself.
